stem: Which pair is an example of bone marrow suppression or infiltration causing acquired neutropenia?

options.text: Benign ethnic neutropenia and metabolic disease
Severe congenital neutropenia and alloimmune neutropenia

explanation: Drugs and aplastic anaemia are examples of acquired neutropenia due to bone marrow suppression or infiltration.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: WBC Disorders

optionExplanations.A: Correct because both drugs and aplastic anaemia are recognised examples of bone marrow suppression or infiltration causing acquired neutropenia.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because benign ethnic neutropenia is a normal variant and metabolic disease is grouped with other genetic or non-marrow causes, not marrow suppression or infiltration.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because severe congenital neutropenia and alloimmune neutropenia are different categories of neutropenia rather than a pair of marrow suppression or infiltration examples.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because asthma and eczema are not causes of acquired neutropenia and are unrelated to marrow suppression or infiltration.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because haemophilia and von Willebrand disease are bleeding disorders, not causes of acquired neutropenia.
